h: קוּנְטְרֵס עֲמֵלָהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה, ג׳ Kuntres Amalah Shel Torah, 3
Matzah, the Food of Healing: Rectifying the Root of Desire

p: which is called in the Zohar
for what it is a healing.
for the wound of the world's blow,
according to the view that it was wheat.
And when one eats this food
to fulfill the mitzvah of Hashem,
the Resurrection of the Dead will be on Pesach,
and then death will be swallowed up forever,
"The wolf and the lamb shall graze together," etc.
had the decree fall upon them,
even though they have no understanding;
for they are no better than man,
for whose sake they were all created;
who brought the creatures down to the dust,
who is the beginning of the corruption,
and it will not avail him
even the most pious of the pious
because he died only through the counsel of the serpent;
for there was nothing in him
but that filth of the serpent
so that he was not as man will be in the future;
(מִדְרַשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם, זֹהַר חֵלֶק א קלז, ב)
"And I will give you a heart of flesh":
וְכֵן עַל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And likewise about Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
"Even the lowest of the low," etc.,
"rather he intended to bring forth offspring";
no sense of personal pleasure at all;
like Adam HaRishon before the sin,
brought this desire into him as well,
then even those long dead will live,
for it will be rectified retroactively as well.
And this is what is written,
"I put to death and I give life;
I have wounded and I will heal":
that He will heal the wound of the world's blow.
and it says, "and whom I have harmed,"
in whom there is no yetzer hara;
and therefore it is called "bread of affliction."
And regarding the mann, too, it says,
"He afflicted you and let you hunger
for "a full belly breeds wicked deeds"
there was no filling of the belly,
like the eating of a poor man
who has not enough to eat his fill
which was given to those who ate the mann;
for such is the way of Torah:
and not for those who chase after desires.
And likewise the mitzvah of eating matzah
like all the mitzvos over which we bless,
"Who sanctified us with His mitzvos and commanded us,"
and it is said, "Sanctify us with Your mitzvos";
into all of a person's eating,
in the way they said of the mann
what the merchants of the nations sold
And it is a preparation for receiving the Torah,
so that he can grasp the Tree of Life —
"and eat" of its bread "and live forever."
And the Resurrection of the Dead, too,
that the dew of Torah revives;
and at the Giving of the Torah,
it is stated in Perek Rabbi Akiva
that HaKadosh Baruch Hu brought out the dew
with which He will revive the dead in the future,
for their souls departed when He spoke;
for the physical body of this world
And the Torah is also a healing,
"It shall be healing for your navel";
and from the very beginning of his formation;
for from where is the fetus formed?
That is, by virtue of his root
for the souls of all the generations
as they said in Shemos Rabbah (Shemos Rabbah 40:3):
"Where were you when I founded the earth?" —
in what place were you hanging
For some hung from his nose and some, etc.;
and three hundred sixty-five spiritual sinews,
corresponding to which are the 613 mitzvos of the Torah,
And on the side of holiness,
And likewise, when man ruled over man
"Your father — in what was he most careful?"
for according to the root of each person,
belonging to that limb and sinew,
in which he must be especially careful.
in whatever matter he is sunk
should know that in it he is prepared
and subdues the force of evil
from the serpent's filth within him;
Whoever is greater than his fellow,
And this is the healing for the root
And the root of all the particular forces of evil
is in the desire for eating,
which is the beginning of the entry of evil,
and from this one comes afterward
For even the inclination to anger and murder,
which is the opposite of desire,
after the filth of desire had entered,
and wanted to inherit the whole world.
And it is stated in Shabbos (Shabbos 105b)
and in Niddah (Niddah 13b, at the top)
that such is the craft of the yetzer hara:
For even the inclination to idolatry
only to permit themselves forbidden relations.
And the holy eating of matzah
is the going out from their filth,
"and their issue is like the issue of horses."
And for this were all the plagues:
to weaken the force of evil
so that Yisrael would be able
for they were enslaved to the evil,
even though he knows that its end is bad:
"Sweet to a man is the bread of falsehood,
And there is no free man
except one who engages in Torah,
to any thing or bodily desire.
and from darkness to great light, etc.
And about this it is said,
the spread of the filth of desires.
And it says, "I will not place upon you":
and consequently the sickness of Mitzrayim will not come,
for once the root has already been healed
there is no room for spreading.
And this is the healing that is needed
even when there is no sickness,
for there is already a deficiency
at the root and from birth
that they set the blessing of healing as the eighth
which requires healing, is on the eighth day.
even when there is no sickness,
is for the healing of the root;
for this is the essential healing.
And it is physically in the body,
which is named after the nations of the world —
is the root of the filth of desire
that issues from the skin of the serpent.
serves to weaken the force of desire.
so would all his descendants after him have been.
But when he sinned, they said
that his foreskin was drawn forward;
for his foreskin was drawn forward
through the filth of the serpent,
נוֹלְדוּ כָּל זַרְעוֹ גַּם כֵּן עֲרֵלִים,
all his descendants too were born uncircumcised,
עַד שֶׁבָּא אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
until Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him, came
and took hold of the holiness of this attribute,
to completing the full stature of his holiness —
which is at one hundred years,
the level of rectifying desire completely
and rectifying the filth of Adam HaRishon —
which is the removal of that filth;
and through this he would be "whole,"
and his stature would be completed in perfection.
and an uncircumcised man is forbidden to eat the Pesach offering;
serves to rectify the desire for eating,
for there is no joy except with meat;
and when he gorges on meat
from this he will come to every kind of evil.
Therefore in the wilderness there was forbidden
and "they buried the people who craved"
as it was said to Adam HaRishon,
And to Adam HaRishon before the sin,
nor was he warned about it;
for, as appears from the passage
where it says, "And He planted," etc.,
"and He placed the man there," etc.,
it is not mentioned at all
וְאִם כֵּן לֹא הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ
and if so, it was not possible for him
that He did not want to test him with this,
for if he were to transgress it,
the overpowering of desire would be so great
that it would be hard to rectify
before the Giving of the Torah,
for he did not yet have
solely as healing for the yetzer,
and there is no other healing for it.
וְרַק עַל יְדֵי אֲכִילַת עֵץ הַדַּעַת,
And only through eating of the Tree of Knowledge,
from partaking of the evil part within it,
and only of the good part;
they would have sunk deeply into desire,
עַד שֶׁלֹּא יָכְלוּ לָצֵאת מִזֶּה כְּלָל,
until they could not get out of it at all,
in His abundant mercy and kindness,
for He desires the well-being of His creatures,
and his descendants after him until Noach,
so that they did not stumble also in eating meat.
and rectified somewhat the sin of Adam HaRishon,
to lessen the curse of the ground
(for this too was for man's good:
since he was in great sorrow,
they thereby refrained of their own accord
from eating meat, which brings joy),
when he remained the father of the world
and all his descendants were born
was saved from the generation of the Flood;
presumably he did not sin as they did,
for he was the seed of Noach,
in whom the rectification had already somewhat begun
from the sin of Adam HaRishon —
וְעַל כֵּן הוּתַּר לוֹ אֲכִילַת בָּשָׂר,
therefore eating meat was permitted to him,
for there was no longer concern
that he would sink too deeply through it.
also one of the drinkers of wine.
And therefore in the wilderness as well,
before the words of Torah were absorbed within them
and from the remnants of the offerings,
when they began to enter into holiness
they were commanded regarding the bread of affliction,
which is the removal of desire by way of subduing it;
is by way of transforming it:
for meat is the eating of desire,
except that this is the eating of a mitzvah,
and it brings still more holiness into the heart.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Kuntres Es HaOchel 10 — “In the Zohar matzah is called ‘the food of healing’ (II 40b), for it has the power to heal what came before; and so with every mitzvah, as stated above from the Midrash Rabbah… as it is written of words of Torah, ‘It shall be healing to your navel’ (Mishlei 3:8).” Connection: The same Zohar on matzah as the food of healing, which Rav Tzadok explains here as healing the root of desire.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 55b — "Was she the daughter of Nachash? Was she not the daughter of Yishai, as it is written, 'and their sisters were Tzeruyah and Avigail' (I Divrei HaYamim 2:16)? Rather, she was the daughter of one who died only through the counsel of the serpent." Rashi: through the serpent's counsel to Chavah, not through any sin of his own.

paragraphs.text: Taanis 5b — "Rabbi Yochanan said: Yaakov Avinu did not die. He was asked: Was it for nothing that the eulogizers eulogized, the embalmers embalmed and the buriers buried? He answered: I am expounding a verse, as it says, 'And you, fear not, My servant Yaakov… for behold, I save you from afar, and your seed from the land of their captivity' (Yirmeyahu 30:10) — it compares him to his seed: just as his seed is alive, so too he is alive." Rashi: he lives forever; they embalmed him because they thought he had died.

paragraphs.text: Kiddushin 30b — "I created the evil inclination; I created Torah as its antidote… The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: My son, if this repulsive one accosts you, drag him to the beis midrash: if he is stone, he will melt; if he is iron, he will shatter, as it says, 'Is not My word like fire, says Hashem, and like a hammer that shatters rock?' (Yirmeyahu 23:29)." Rashi: "this repulsive one" is the evil inclination provoking you.

paragraphs.text: Yoma 75b — "'Man ate the bread of the mighty (abirim)' (Tehillim 78:25) — bread that the ministering angels eat; the words of Rabbi Akiva. When this was said before Rabbi Yishmael, he said: Go and tell Akiva: Akiva, you erred! Do the ministering angels eat bread? Is it not said, 'I did not eat bread or drink water' (Devarim 9:9)? Rather, 'abirim' means bread absorbed in the 248 limbs (evarim)."

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 88b — "Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: At each utterance that came from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He, the souls of Israel left them, as it says, 'My soul went out when He spoke' (Shir HaShirim 5:6). If their souls left at the first utterance, how did they receive the second? He brought down the dew with which He will revive the dead in the future and revived them, as it says, 'A generous rain You shed, O God' (Tehillim 68:10)."

An old man came and taught him: Whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than he." Rashi: he was speaking of himself.

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 105b — "One who tears his garments in his anger, breaks his vessels in his anger, or scatters his money in his anger should be in your eyes like an idolater; for such is the craft of the evil inclination: today it tells him 'do this,' tomorrow 'do that,' until it tells him 'go worship idols,' and he goes and worships."
